land.text: the Ecuadorian coast from Esmeraldas to Tumbes: Guayas, Santa Elena, Manabí, most of Los Ríos, El Oro, Cañar and part of Esmeraldas

predecessors.note: Spanish colonial province of Guayaquil (Audiencia of Quito); the page does not name the viceroyalty.

land.text: 'On July 31, 1822, the Free Province of Guayaquil declared its official annexation to' Gran Colombia

successors.note: The Free Province page also says Tumbes (now Peru) was in the province.

correction.text: the province 'covered the Ecuadorian coast from Esmeraldas to Tumbes': Guayas, Santa Elena, Manabí, most of Los Ríos, El Oro, Cañar and part of Esmeraldas

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria's 'Guayaquil Junta' row (1812-1813) is a different, earlier shape. The infobox gives 53,000 km2 and a population of 70,000 in 1822; the drawn shape is the union of whole modern provinces, whereas the page says 'part of Esmeraldas' and 'most of Los Ríos', so it may overstate the infobox area: the gazetteer resolves the union to 237 cells, about 59,900 km2, against 53,000 km2 (ratio 1.13, within the factor of two). Tumbes (now Peru) is named in the text but left out of the shape.

region.text: Guayaquil, where 'the independence revolution in Guayaquil on October 9, 1820' began

ledger.note: 9 October 1820: Guayaquil rises against Spain. 'After the independence revolution in Guayaquil on October 9, 1820, several municipalities immediately joined'; the Provisional Government Regulations of 8 November 1820 begin 'The State of Guayaquil is free and independent; its religion is Catholic'.

region.text: the coast from Esmeraldas to Tumbes as the neighbouring municipalities 'immediately joined'

ledger.note: Late 1820: the municipalities of the coast join Guayaquil. The page says 'several municipalities immediately joined' and that the province covered the coast from Esmeraldas to Tumbes; it gives no dates for each, so the land is the infobox extent and the year is 1820. (Reviewer am-08-x, 2026-10-19: month 10 and placed after the found event: 'After the independence revolution in Guayaquil on October 9, 1820, several municipalities immediately joined'.)

region.text: the Free Province of Guayaquil, annexed to Gran Colombia

ledger.note: 31 July 1822: Guayaquil is annexed to Gran Colombia. 'On July 31, 1822, the Free Province of Guayaquil declared its official annexation to' Gran Colombia, after Bolívar's arrival on 11 July and the Guayaquil Conference of 27 July.
July 1822: the free province ends in Gran Colombia. Infobox last leader: Bolívar, 1822; Olmedo had led in 1820 and again in 1821-1822.

wars.name: Guayaquil's independence and the Quito campaign
wars.outcome: Independence confirmed: the page says Guayaquil's emancipation was 'completed ... on May 24, 1822, in the Battle of Pichincha'; the province then joins Gran Colombia on 31 July 1822.
wars.note: The page records no territorial fighting inside the province, so no contest zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The page gives provinces by their modern names, no treaty or survey line; the southern end at Tumbes is approximate.

sources.title: Free Province of Guayaquil
sources.note: Revolution 9 October 1820, Provisional Government Regulations 8 November 1820, extent from Esmeraldas to Tumbes, infobox area 53,000 km2, Pichincha 24 May 1822, annexation 31 July 1822.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for the Free Province (its Guayaquil Junta row 1812-1813 is a different, earlier state and the am-08-b dossier guayaquil-junta covers it). Only one page was opened (page budget 1-2 for three shapes or fewer); no second page was needed for the dates, but the region is the page's own list of modern provinces.
The page gives the leaders only as Olmedo (first, 1820; again 1821-1822) and Bolívar (last, 1822), so no ruler strip is written. Tumbes (Peru) is part of the page's extent but is not drawn; if the reviewer wants it, add {'admin1':'Tumbes','country':'Peru'}.
Also: the am-08-c dossier gran-colombia could add free-province-of-guayaquil as a predecessor (31 July 1822).
